messages:
kevin: Heads up — re-opening discussion on eviction sensitivity vs priority reservation. Hit an OOM in staging where reservation=15% + low eviction sensitivity still failed during a bursty microbatch. Curious if we should rethink reservation semantics (soft vs hard) and add a tiny emergency pool.

sylvia: +1. Can you paste the repro and the config you were using?

kevin: Repro summary: multi-tenant inference runner, burst from 50->120 concurrent microbatches, KV cache stays warm, host staging fills, eviction barely kicks in because sensitivity threshold was 0.65. Reservation accounting lagged ~80ms and by then mem was full.

kevin: Config snippet we used:
```yaml
evictor:
  sensitivity: 0.65
  backoff_ms: 50
priority_reservation:
  enabled: true
  percent: 15
  accounting_window_ms: 100
```

ashok: That accounting_window is too coarse for microbatch spikes. Two quick notes: (1) reservation should have soft/hard modes — soft reserves only prevent preemption until under contention, hard is enforced via preemptible buffer; (2) we should track reservation_age and apply immediate preemption if a tenant consumes > reserved_percent for >reservation_age.

maria: Also consider a tiny emergency pool (2-5%) that's globally preemptible and only used when reservation accounting misses spikes. That pool could be reclaimed first on overload to avoid tenant-facing OOMs.

sylvia: Love the emergency pool idea. To avoid starvation, make it preemptible for best-effort tenants only and add hysteresis so we don't flip-flop. E.g., require pool usage to stay > 3% for 500ms before we start preempting.

ashok: Agreed. Implementation sketch: 1) reservation modes: soft/hard; 2) emergency_pool_pct default 3; 3) metrics: reservation_utilization, preempt_count_per_tenant, emergency_pool_usage; 4) preempt backoff per-tenant to avoid thrash.

kevin: How about algorithm: if tenant crosses reserved_percent + emergency_pool and persists > T, mark preemptible and try to evict least-recently-used pages from that tenant up to min(preempt_target, tenant_overrun) with exponential backoff if eviction fails. Add a per-tenant 'demote_score' that increments on preempt failures and forces a soft-demotion (lower priority) if above threshold.

maria: That handles thrash but we also need fairness across tenants that sporadically spike. Proposal: give each tenant a small burst window (burst_credit_ms) where they can exceed reservation without penalty; only persistent overruns get penalized.

kevin: Good call. So we combine: burst credit, emergency pool, soft/hard reservation, demote_score, and backoff.

sylvia: For rollout: (A) simulation + historical trace replay (we should reuse the sampling traces from the 2025 stress run), (B) feature-flagged canary with evictor_mode=conservative, (C) collect metrics for 24-72h and check preempt rate and customer error rate.

ashok: Ops will help with replay traces and canary infra. Recommend adding a "simulate" switch server-side to test decisions without actually evicting.

kevin: I'll draft an RFC follow-up with the API surface (config fields + new metrics) and a simulation harness plan. Volunteers to review?

maria: I'll review.

sylvia: Happy to review — will also scope telemetry changes.

ashok: I'll coordinate trace replays and help define eviction test cases.

evictor-bot: Note: created issue INF-2398 for "eviction-reservation-mode-and-emergency-pool" and scheduled a short sync Thu 11:00.

kevin: Perfect. I'll post a link to the RFC draft and include some replay traces as attachments. Thanks all :thumbsup:
